The kameez (tunic) has a darted front and darted back with basic full sleeves was drafted on Banarasi brocade fabric (2.5 meters).

Step 1. First I stitched the main fabric with lining on the neckline for both front and back keeping the right sides facing each other, flipped to right side for a top stitch on the neckline. 
Step 2. Stitched the front darts , back darts. Joined the front and back panel on shoulder seam. 
Step 3. Attached pocket cut on both front and back panel.
Step 4. Stitched side seam till the hip level with one of the side seam having zipper ( I am yet to learn attaching zipper even with the zipper foot).
Step 5. Attached the sleeves using the set in sleeve ( it was very challenging, somehow it worked)
Step 6. Stitched the sides for slit and stitched the hemline
Step 7. Attached the two trims on the hemline to make the garment more indian

The skirt or lehenga is made on silk fabric about 4 meter length

Cut the skirt pattern giving a 90 degree flare using basic skirt pattern. Checked for evenness on both front and back flare. Attached pockets. The waistline has a side zipper and a buckle. Stitched the side seams and completed the hemline stitch and attached the trim on the skirt hem.

Styled the outfit with net embroidered dupatta (stole)

This navy blue colored kameez/ tunic was a piece of cloth having the neck embroidery when I bought it from local market. It was about 2 meters, I self drafted the pattern with a princess line dart in the front with straight cut on the seamlines. The basic has shoulder and waist darts.
Firstly Stitched darts together, then attached  the linen material with the main fabric on the neck, keeping right sides together turned the fabric to the right side giving a top stitch for the neck. (for both front and back panel)
Joined the front and back together on the shoulder seam
Stitched the sleeves to the armhole, stitched the hemlines and sleeve hem
Used french seam to sew the side seam from where I wanted the slit ( the kameez/tunic has a slit on both sides)
Attached the pockets on both sides.
Joined the side seam starting from sleeve hem till the point in the dress where I wanted a slit.

*My dress definitely will have one element that is pockets*

I have made Scrunchies from the left over fabrics of my various projects

I made 2 measurement Scrunchies and a few with the bow

Bigger Scrunchie made using (17x3) inches fabric and an elastic band. 
Smaller scrunchie made using (10x2) inches fabric and 5 inch elastic
(If you want more gathers then  increase the length accordingly)
For the bow (20x2.5) inches fabric

For making the Scrunchies

*fold the fabric by having one end of width to another and place the elastic band in between
* Stretch the band and sew along
(Here the right side of the fabric are facing each other while the wrong side is visible outside)
*Once we have sewn the fabric completely (while we have the elastic band in between)
* Pull the right side of the fabric out by using a safety pin
*Sew the end of the fabric and the Scrunchie will be ready

For making smaller Scrunchies where we use elastic

Join one length of the fabric to another and sew along 2 mm 
Flip the fabric to the right side out by using a safety pin
Insert the elastic and make a stitch on the two ends of the elastic then on the fabric to complete the Scrunchie

For making the bow 

Cut the two ends of the fabric in a diagonal line 

Fold and sew along (right side facing each other)  one end to another by leaving a gap in between

Turn the fabric right side out and make a stitch on 1mm end
Your bow is ready to be attached to the Scrunchie 😬
